title: Quiet Sprint Deployment Chronicle — Jul 2026 (draft)
body:
Purpose:
A compact, low-noise deployment for the July sprint: push runtime patch + routing adjustments to reduce tail latency for small seq lengths. This doc is a working chronicle — combines a lightweight hour-by-hour calendar, preflight checklist, smoke tests, and a draft of release notes for later copy-edit. Intention: keep scope minimal, limit customer-visible risk, and exercise the new canary routing heuristics.

Goals:
- Deploy runtime v2.18.3 with micro-quantization kernel swap (nvfuser opt)
- Validate canary routing policy v1.4 in two regions (us-west1, eu-west1)
- No customer-facing errors >0.1% or latency degradation >10% p95

Stakeholders:
- Oncall owner: Marcus Li
- Release lead: Sofia Patel
- SRE oversight: Aisha Raman
- Product owner: Daniel Cortez

Quiet Sprint — hour-by-hour plan (T=0 is scheduled cutover: 2026-07-14 02:00 UTC)
- T-72h: Final smoke dataset run and nightly perf sweep (obs: low-load token histograms)
- T-24h: Freeze rollout window, announce quiet window in #release-ops, set PagerDuty rota
- T-2h: Canary pods booted in us-west1 (1% traffic), healthchecks green for 15m
- T+0: Shift to canary routing policy v1.4 in us-west1 (1% -> 5% over 10m ramp)
- T+10m: Canary telemetry review (errors, tail-latency histograms, qps distribution)
- T+30m: If stable, expand canary to 20% in us-west1 and start eu-west1 canary at 1%
- T+90m: Target 50% in us-west1, 20% in eu-west1; begin slow ramp to 100% over next 3h only if all signals are nominal
- T+4h: Full routing swap end-state target (or rollback if throttle gates triggered)
- T+24h: Post-rollout retrospective snapshot and regressions check

Preflight checklist (quick pass):
- [ ] Release artifacts built and checksummed (sha256)
- [ ] Canary image pushed to registry and signed
- [ ] Nightly perf baseline attached to this doc (link in linked_artifacts)
- [ ] Telemetry dashboards preconfigured (latency p50/p95/p99, error rate, model fallback counts)
- [ ] Rollback image identified and tested
- [ ] Communication draft to customers (if any regressions) prepared in /docs/release-notes

Deployment playbook (stepwise, operator notes):
- Operator boots canary (k8s job): record pod ids, node allocation, GPU type in the watchlog
- Verify KV cache warmup profile within 15m (sample prefixes)
- Confirm continuous batching latency bucket not increasing for small seq lengths
- If error spike >0.1% in 5m window OR p95 increase >20% -> immediate scale-down to previous routing and open incident channel (#inc-quiet-sprint)
- Use traffic knob to shift traffic in 5% increments, hold 10m between increments for signal sampling

Smoke tests (runnable commands / expectations):
- short-seq-gen.sh against canary endpoint (expect median latency within 10% of baseline)
- long-streaming-check.py for function calls (no more than 1% failed calls)
- embedding-regress-check.rb (sample 2000 vectors) -> cosine distribution should not drift by >0.02 on average

Draft release notes (working copy — will be cleaned before publish):
- Runtime: v2.18.3 — swaps micro-quant kernels to nvfuser-opt path, reduces CPU overhead on hybrid instances. Expected: 6–12% token-cost reduction for small sequences.
- Routing: canary routing policy v1.4 — introduces gradual ramp with regional awareness to reduce cross-region fallbacks. Known limitations: heavy long-seq workloads may see no perf improvement.
- Operational: improved autoscaler cooldown for dedicated pools (config toggle).

Known risks & mitigations:
- Risk: kernel swap could expose cache alignment bug on older drivers. Mitigation: conservative canary + node-type exclusion list (exclude gtx-1x legacy nodes).
- Risk: under-sampled telemetry in first 30m -> mitigation: increase sampling windows to 100% for small seq requests for canary pods for 30m only.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Do we want to coordinate a light customer advisory for high-volume partners? (action: Daniel to decide by T-24h)
- Confirm whether onprem package needs separate rollout window (Aisha to confirm compatibility matrix)
- Add a short-run deterministic eval (RNG seed) to smoke sequence generator to detect subtle output drift (Marcus assigned)

Post-deploy notes template (for quick paste into the release digest):
- T+4h: rollout completed to us-west1 and eu-west1 (metrics: errors 0.03%, p95 latency -3% vs baseline).
- T+24h: follow-up perf sweep attached, no regressions in embedding quality detected.
- Action items: revert exclusion list to default, update release checklist with new smoke test command.

Field notes / informal log (snapshots while running):
- 2026-07-14 01:46 UTC: night-run flagged one old-node with driver mismatch; node excluded from canary pool.
- 2026-07-14 02:18 UTC: canary p95 slightly elevated (+8%) for 3m — traced to batching thrash on a new kernel, held ramp and increased sampling; resolved after cache warmup.
- 2026-07-14 05:10 UTC: expanded to 50% in us-west1, no customer-visible errors.

Usage notes for next time:
- Add explicit driver-version gate to preflight; automate node-type exclusion via labels
- Keep a short deterministic eval in smoke suite; it catches drift faster than quality heuristics

If anything changes during the window, paste this doc into #release-ops and update the field notes section in real time.

End of draft chronicle.
